clue.text: Star depressed at end of day

blocks.note: the Sun is the star our planet circles
someone depressed is feeling down

explanation.surface: A celebrity feeling low as the working day draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' reads as a famous person with the blues; here it is the literal star in the sky, and 'depressed' says where it has sunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is the moment the sun sets, which is the end of the day.

clue.text: Crazy Scary Spice's first to go "Vulgar!"

indicators.note: the first letter of the word leaves, so SCARY loses its S
crazy letters are jumbled out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of Spice, which is also the letter that goes from SCARY, leaving CARY

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl losing her head and yelling that something is vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Scary Spice was Mel B of the Spice Girls, but the name is only letters here: drop the S and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy jokes are risqué and a little vulgar.

clue.text: Vulnerability caused by degraded sulphur added to drug

blocks.note: something degraded has been made weaker
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab warning about cut sulphur mixed into a drug making someone vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Added to' puts the drug after the sulphur, so the pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak spot is a point where something can be attacked: a vulnerability.

clue.text: Chap, or a yet to be reformed old drug dealer

indicators.note: letters that are reformed are shaped into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fellow, once a drug pusher, who has not yet gone straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' suggests a criminal; the 'old' one is a respectable pharmacist of past centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was the historical name for a person who prepared and sold medicines.

clue.text: Oakeshott, a waffler, "protecting" capital

indicators.note: the outer words protect the answer by wrapping round it

blocks.note: the letters run from the last three of the surname, across the lone 'a', into the first two of the next word

explanation.surface: A jibe at Isabel Oakeshott, the political journalist, as a windbag guarding her money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money being protected; it is a capital city. The quotation marks around 'protecting' flag that the word is doing crossword work.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Canadian seat of government is one of the world's capital cities.

clue.text: Kip, put away organ!

blocks.note: to shut something away is to put it away
the eye is an organ of sight

explanation.surface: A cheeky command to go to sleep and put away a certain body part.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for a sleep. The exclamation mark and 'organ' invite a ruder reading; the organ is only the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for sleep, just as kip is.

clue.text: Out of bed, whip is feeling optimistic

blocks.note: someone out of bed is up
to whip is to beat

explanation.surface: A party whip who has got up and is in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Private Eye 'whip' suggests the parliamentary enforcer; here it is the verb, as in whipping eggs or a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word describes a cheerful, hopeful mood, borrowed from the lively unaccented beat in music.

clue.text: Wall built by Republicans that is put in check

indicators.note: the letters before it are put inside the word that follows

blocks.note: R for Republican, doubled for the plural
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, 'that is'
to check someone's progress is to bar it

explanation.surface: Trump's border wall, erected by Republicans and meant to keep people in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural matters: one Republican would be a single R, but 'Republicans' needs two.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall is one kind of obstacle built to stop people passing, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Message: "Pad chest out"

indicators.note: letters knocked out of place come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A curt note telling a bodybuilder to bulk up his chest with padding.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Message' look like a heading for the quoted text; it is the definition, and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A despatch is an official message, as sent from a war correspondent or envoy.

clue.text: se 28dn.
Tarnished Labour's disagreeable task

blocks.note: something tarnished is dirty
labour is work

explanation.surface: A sideswipe at the scandal-hit Labour Party and the grubby job it has to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour the political party; it is only labour, meaning work. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase names the unpleasant or underhand job someone else is made to do.

clue.text: Drink to Brown

blocks.note: raising a glass in someone's honour
the verb: to crisp bread under a grill

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B suggests Gordon Brown, the former Labour prime minister; it is the verb, as in browning bread under a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast means both to drink someone's health and to brown something by heat.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) The KKK is fine with this pale creamy soup cooked with nothing taken out

definitions.text: The KKK is fine with this

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
a letter taken out is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: white is the palest colour
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing; it leaves CREAMYSUP to be cooked

explanation.surface: A menu note about a bland white soup of which the Ku Klux Klan would approve.
explanation.walkthrough: The soup sounds like a dish description, but the pale white is the first word and the soup's letters, minus the O, make the second. The answer runs on into 15 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ku Klux Klan is a white supremacist group, so white supremacy is what it endorses.

clue.text: Our mag covers pirate wear

blocks.note: the clue appears in Private Eye, so 'our mag' is the Eye
a patch covers a hole or a wound

explanation.surface: The magazine's front covers showing pirates' outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like magazine covers; it is the plural noun meaning patches.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch over one eye is the classic accessory of the storybook pirate.

clue.text: see 13ac.
In particular, restrain bust

indicators.note: the answer is in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the last two of the first word into the first four of the second

explanation.surface: Advice to hold back one's bosom in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' pretends to be the chest; it is police slang for an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: when the police bust someone they take them into custody.

clue.text: Aspect of LBGTQ legislation? "Carry Out!"

blocks.note: the T of the initialism stands for transgender, and a piece of legislation is an act
to conduct a piece of business

explanation.surface: A demand to take something away, perhaps a gay-rights law.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented reading TRANS ACT; the clue's LBGTQ is a slip for LGBTQ.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct or carry out a piece of business.

clue.text: Journey of one who scored after midnight, finally

indicators.note: the composer comes after the T
the final letter of midnight

blocks.note: the last letter of midnight
Maurice Ravel, the French composer who wrote the score of Boléro

explanation.surface: A late-night trip home for someone who scored a goal, or got lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' suggests goals or a sexual conquest; it means wrote music.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun for going from place to place, as in 'air travel'.

clue.text: Old lover was a crossword setter, reportedly? Leave it out!

definitions.note: The definition is the imperative 'leave it out', a British phrase for stop that; the answer's sense is to leave out.

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a former partner is an ex
a crossword setter clued the answers

explanation.surface: Someone's former partner turned out to be a puzzle compiler, to which the listener says 'Don't be ridiculous!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave it out!' is British slang for 'give over' or 'stop it', which makes it sound like a reaction rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once the slang is set aside: to omit or keep something off a list.

clue.text: When there's less demand from Dicky to climax

blocks.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, and so is off
a climax is a peak

explanation.surface: A smutty line about a man named Dicky reaching climax at a quiet time.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D makes Dicky a name, or something ruder; it is the adjective, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak hours are the times when demand for travel or power is lower.

clue.text: Bossy, say, crazy dude with DTs

indicators.note: crazy letters are jumbled out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder

explanation.surface: A domineering, deranged man suffering the DTs, the shakes of alcohol withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bossy' reads as domineering; here it means covered in bosses, the raised knobs on a shield, and 'say' marks it as one example of being studded.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosses are round studs, so a bossy surface is studded with them.

clue.text: Trump's third term out of consideration, causing collapse

blocks.note: the American word for autumn, the third season after spring and summer
something set apart, as in 'joking apart', is left out of consideration

explanation.surface: A warning that a third Trump term, though ruled out, would bring the country down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' suggests a presidential term of office; it means a word, and Trump's American word for the third season is FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a structure, a marriage or a government that crumbles to pieces has collapsed.

clue.text: Sexual urge of old politician dominating one party

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that dominates sits on top

blocks.note: a Liberal, from the party that merged into today's Liberal Democrats
I is the Roman numeral one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The lust of an old politician dominating a party, a familiar Private Eye story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dominating' puts LIB above the rest, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: Freud's Latin word for desire became the everyday term for sex drive.

clue.text: Tough getting handjob outside hospital?

indicators.note: the word goes outside the letter that follows

blocks.note: tug is British slang for a handjob
H is the hospital sign

explanation.surface: A lewd scene outside a hospital that is a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' is not the adjective but the noun, a tough being a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a hired heavy or street hoodlum is a tough.

clue.text: Time to abandon stupid, chatty billionaire's plaything?

indicators.note: the letter for time abandons the word, leaving it behind
stupid letters are muddled out of their proper order

blocks.note: T is the symbol for time
taken as written; one T goes, leaving CHATY

explanation.surface: A dig at a daft, talkative billionaire, and the time he should give up his toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' and 'chatty' look like insults for the billionaire; one is the anagram signal and the other the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A superyacht is the classic toy of the very rich.

clue.text: Bush-like purge of left from the people

indicators.note: a purge gets rid of something, here the letter for left
the letter is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the general population, a six-letter word that then loses its L

explanation.surface: A political purge of the left in the style of George W. Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bush a president; the bush is pubic hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is slang for a mass of pubic hair, so bush-like things are pubic.

clue.text: South Dakota entertains profuse pleasure for Trump-style money-raising?

definitions.note: The definition is an activity, while the answer is the pot of money such raising fills.

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside the house, so SD holds the other letters

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
lush growth is profuse
fun is pleasure

explanation.surface: A South Dakota fundraiser laying on lavish treats for donors, Trump style.
explanation.walkthrough: The American state sets the scene of a campaign fundraiser, but it only supplies the outer S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is a secret stash of money used for improper purposes, such as political dirty tricks.

clue.text: (& 10dn.) I'm just starting to see her go off

indicators.note: letters gone off have spoiled and lost their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone about to watch a woman set off.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 10 down.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'here goes' as they begin something daunting.

clue.text: House due a nice transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes the letters' order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A property overdue for a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a home in need of work; in the theatre the house is the audience, as in a full house.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the house means the people watching.

clue.text: Cheese's said to produce wind

indicators.note: a word that is said is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese blamed for giving someone wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as flatulence after the cheese; it is only a light breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the light, pleasant kind of moving air.
